components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 逃 is to run away.
兆 (zhào) — loose hint — 逃 is táo; 兆 also sounds out 桃 táo (same sound) and 跳 tiào.
犭 (beast, form of 犬 dog) — animals: 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf; 犯 is to attack or violate, hence offend.

example.hanzi: 警方悬赏抓捕那名逃犯。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng xuánshǎng zhuōbǔ nà míng táofàn.
example.english: The police offered a reward for capturing that fugitive.
example.fact: D. B. Cooper hijacked a Boeing 727 in 1971, extorted $200,000 in ransom, and parachuted from the plane over the Pacific Northwest. Despite one of the longest manhunts in FBI history, he was never identified or found.

examples.hanzi: 那名逃犯已经被抓回来了。
examples.pinyin: Nà míng táofàn yǐjīng bèi zhuā huílái le.
examples.english: That fugitive has already been caught.

examples.hanzi: 有人看见逃犯往北边跑了。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu rén kànjiàn táofàn wǎng běibian pǎo le.
examples.english: Someone saw the fugitive run toward the north.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money, as in 买, 费, 贵; 财 is wealth.
才 (cái) — same sound — 财 is cái, like 才; 才 also sounds out 材 cái.
攵 (tap, hand with stick) — acts that direct others: 教 teach, 放 release, 改 change, 收 collect; 政 is governing.
正 (zhèng) is the same sound; fits the sense too — government puts things right.

example.hanzi: 政府正在讨论明年的财政预算。
example.pinyin: zhèngfǔ zhèngzài tǎolùn míngnián de cáizhèng yùsuàn.
example.english: The government is discussing next year's fiscal budget.
example.fact: The Bank of England, founded in 1694 to help fund a war against France, is considered one of the first institutions to formalize modern government deficit financing by selling long-term bonds to the public.

examples.hanzi: 这个城市的财政收入每年都在增长。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì de cáizhèng shōurù měi nián dōu zài zēngzhǎng.
examples.english: This city's fiscal revenue grows every year.

examples.hanzi: 学校的财政状况不太好。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào de cáizhèng zhuàngkuàng bú tài hǎo.
examples.english: The school's financial situation is not very good.

components.note: 心 (heart) — marks feelings and thought, as in 想 think, 念 miss, 感 feel; 愁 is worry or sorrow.
秋 (qiū) — close sound: 愁 chóu. 秋 also sounds out 揪 jiū.

example.hanzi: 她为钱的事发愁。
example.pinyin: Tā wèi qián de shì fāchóu.
example.english: She is worried about money.
example.fact: 愁 gives 发愁 (to worry), 愁眉苦脸 (a gloomy face) and 乡愁 (homesickness). Poetry links autumn (秋) with melancholy, which fits the 秋 (autumn) inside this character.

examples.hanzi: 她为孩子的学习发愁。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèi háizi de xuéxí fāchóu.
examples.english: She worries about her child's studies.

examples.hanzi: 你别愁眉苦脸的，事情会好的。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié chóuméi kǔliǎn de, shìqing huì hǎo de.
examples.english: Don't look so troubled, things will get better.

components.note: 冫 (ice, two drops) — marks cold and freezing, as in 冷 cold, 冻 freeze, 凉 cool; 冰 is 冫 plus 水 water: frozen water.
土 (earth) — a lump of earth; also in 地 ground, 城 city.
夬 (guài) is a loose clue; 快 kuài shares it and sounds exactly like 块.

example.hanzi: 请在我的饮料里加些冰块。
example.pinyin: qǐng zài wǒ de yǐnliào lǐ jiā xiē bīngkuài.
example.english: Please add some ice cubes to my drink.
example.fact: Before mechanical refrigeration became common in the 20th century, 19th-century entrepreneurs such as Frederic Tudor built a global 'ice trade,' cutting blocks of ice from frozen New England ponds and shipping them by sea as far as India and the Caribbean.

examples.hanzi: 夏天我喜欢喝加冰块的柠檬水。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān wǒ xǐhuan hē jiā bīngkuài de níngméngshuǐ.
examples.english: In summer I like lemonade with ice cubes.

examples.hanzi: 冰箱里的冰块已经用完了。
examples.pinyin: Bīngxiāng lǐ de bīngkuài yǐjīng yòngwán le.
examples.english: The ice cubes in the fridge are all used up.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 依 is to lean on someone.
衣 (yī) — same sound — 依 is yī, like 衣.
旧 (simplified 舊) — old; the old sound part 臼 (jiù) also gives 舅 jiù (uncle).

example.hanzi: 多年过去了,他依旧住在那个小镇。
example.pinyin: duō nián guòqùle, tā yījiù zhù zài nàge xiǎozhèn.
example.english: Many years have passed, and he still lives in that small town.
example.fact: General Sherman, a giant sequoia in California's Sequoia National Park, is estimated to be around 2,200 years old and remains the largest known tree on Earth by volume, having grown slowly but steadily for millennia.

examples.hanzi: 过了二十年，他依旧很爱她。
examples.pinyin: Guò le èrshí nián, tā yījiù hěn ài tā.
examples.english: Twenty years later, he still loves her.

examples.hanzi: 虽然下着雨，大家依旧去爬山了。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán xiàzhe yǔ, dàjiā yījiù qù pá shān le.
examples.english: Even though it was raining, everyone still went hiking.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and roles: 你, 他, 位; 使 is sending someone to do something.
吏 (lì, official) gives the meaning, and shares its ancestor 史 (shǐ), the exact sound of 使.
者 (zhě) is a sound clue for 都 dū, 著 zhù, 煮 zhǔ, 猪 zhū and 诸 zhū; as a word it means "one who", as in 作者 author.

example.hanzi: 那位使者带来了国王的口信。
example.pinyin: nà wèi shǐzhě dàiláile guówáng de kǒuxìn.
example.english: That envoy brought a message from the king.
example.fact: According to legend, the Greek messenger Pheidippides ran roughly 40 kilometers from the battlefield of Marathon to Athens in 490 BC to announce a Greek victory over Persia, collapsing after delivering the news. The modern marathon race is named after his run.

examples.hanzi: 他是和平的使者，到处宣传友谊。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì hépíng de shǐzhě, dàochù xuānchuán yǒuyì.
examples.english: He is a messenger of peace who promotes friendship everywhere.

examples.hanzi: 邻国派使者来参加庆典。
examples.pinyin: Línguó pài shǐzhě lái cānjiā qìngdiǎn.
examples.english: The neighboring country sent an envoy to the celebration.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — the sheep family: 美, 养, 群. Dictionary story: work 工 done by a sheep — memory aid for being poor or off. Origin uncertain.
工 (work) — the bottom. Memory aid: poor work 工, so 差劲 poor quality. 差 is chā/chà (difference, lacking) or chāi (send).
刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 刻; to cut apart means separate.
另 (lìng, other) — separating things into "other" parts: 别 is another, different, or "don't".

example.hanzi: 这两种材料的价格有很大差别。
example.pinyin: zhè liǎng zhǒng cáiliào de jiàgé yǒu hěn dà chābié.
example.english: There is a big price difference between these two materials.
example.fact: Identical twins share nearly all of their DNA at birth, yet studies show that environmental and epigenetic differences accumulate over a lifetime, causing their gene expression patterns to diverge more and more as they age even though their genomes remain the same.

examples.hanzi: 这两个城市的生活水平差别很大。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè chéngshì de shēnghuó shuǐpíng chābié hěn dà.
examples.english: The living standards in these two cities differ greatly.

examples.hanzi: 双胞胎之间几乎没有什么差别。
examples.pinyin: Shuāngbāotāi zhījiān jīhū méiyǒu shénme chābié.
examples.english: There is hardly any difference between the twins.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 遗 is leaving something behind or losing it.
贵 (valuable) — what is precious is what you regret leaving behind or what is left to heirs.
廾 (two hands) — hands throwing something out: 弃 is to cast away.

example.hanzi: 这只小狗被主人遗弃在路边。
example.pinyin: zhè zhī xiǎo gǒu bèi zhǔrén yíqì zài lùbiān.
example.english: This little dog was abandoned by its owner on the roadside.
example.fact: The Chernobyl Exclusion Zone in Ukraine has been largely abandoned by humans since the 1986 nuclear disaster, yet wildlife populations there — including wolves, lynx, and wild horses — have rebounded in the decades since, thriving in the absence of human activity.

examples.hanzi: 法律禁止遗弃老人和孩子。
examples.pinyin: Fǎlǜ jìnzhǐ yíqì lǎorén hé háizi.
examples.english: The law forbids abandoning the elderly and children.

examples.hanzi: 他从不遗弃自己养的宠物。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng bù yíqì zìjǐ yǎng de chǒngwù.
examples.english: He never abandons the pets he keeps.

components.note: 缶 (clay jar) — marks pots and jars, as in 罐 jar, 缸 vat; a chipped jar is 缺, lacking.
夬 (guài/jué) is a loose hint for quē; 决 jué and 快 kuài share it.
阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阳, 院; 陷 is falling into a pit.
臽 (xiàn) — same sound — 陷 is xiàn; 臽 also sounds out 馅 xiàn.

example.hanzi: 这批产品被发现存在设计缺陷。
example.pinyin: zhè pī chǎnpǐn bèi fāxiàn cúnzài shèjì quēxiàn.
example.english: This batch of products was found to have a design defect.
example.fact: The original Tacoma Narrows Bridge in Washington state collapsed in 1940, just months after opening, when wind-induced oscillations exposed a fatal flaw in its slender, flexible deck. The disaster reshaped modern bridge engineering and aerodynamic testing.

examples.hanzi: 这件衣服有个小缺陷，所以打折了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu yǒu gè xiǎo quēxiàn, suǒyǐ dǎzhé le.
examples.english: This garment has a small flaw, so it's discounted.

examples.hanzi: 每个人都有自己的缺陷。
examples.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yǒu zìjǐ de quēxiàn.
examples.english: Everyone has their own shortcomings.

components.note: 火 (fire) — a picture of flames, and a component seen in 烧, 灯, 热 (as the dots 灬), 炒; fire radical for burning and heat.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 这支军队拥有强大的火力。
example.pinyin: zhè zhī jūnduì yǒngyǒu qiángdà de huǒlì.
example.english: This army possesses powerful firepower.
example.fact: The Gatling gun, patented in 1862, is often cited as one of the first practical rapid-fire weapons, capable of firing several hundred rounds per minute. It foreshadowed the machine guns that would come to dominate 20th-century warfare.

examples.hanzi: 炮兵的火力压住了对方的进攻。
examples.pinyin: Pàobīng de huǒlì yāzhù le duìfāng de jìngōng.
examples.english: The artillery's firepower held back the enemy's attack.

examples.hanzi: 灶上的火力太大，菜都煮糊了。
examples.pinyin: Zào shàng de huǒlì tài dà, cài dōu zhǔ hú le.
examples.english: The heat on the stove was too high, and the dish got burnt.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
人 (person) — the top part. 个 is the general measure word, as in 一个, 这个, 那个.
丨 (a vertical tally) — under 人, read as one tally mark per person: counting individuals one by one.
月 — a crescent moon, also the word for month; in body words ⺼ is a different part, as in 脸 face.

example.hanzi: 上个月我们去北京旅游了。
example.pinyin: shàng gè yuè wǒmen qù Běijīng lǚyóule.
example.english: Last month we traveled to Beijing.
example.fact: The Gregorian calendar, introduced by Pope Gregory XIII in 1582 to correct drift in the older Julian calendar, is the calendar most widely used today. Some countries, notably Russia, did not adopt it until the 20th century.

examples.hanzi: 上个月我换了一份新工作。
examples.pinyin: Shàng gè yuè wǒ huàn le yí fèn xīn gōngzuò.
examples.english: Last month I changed to a new job.

examples.hanzi: 这家店上个月刚开业。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn shàng gè yuè gāng kāiyè.
examples.english: This shop only opened last month.

components.note: 火 (fire) — a picture of flames, and a component seen in 烧, 灯, 热 (as the dots 灬), 炒; fire radical for burning and heat.
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body parts, as in 脚 foot, 脸 face.
退 (tuì) gives the same syllable with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 早餐我常常吃火腿三明治。
example.pinyin: zǎocān wǒ chángcháng chī huǒtuǐ sānmíngzhì.
example.english: For breakfast I often eat a ham sandwich.
example.fact: Parma ham, or prosciutto di Parma, must by Italian law be cured for at least 12 months using only salt and time, with no nitrates or other preservatives permitted under its protected designation of origin.

examples.hanzi: 火腿和鸡蛋是很常见的早餐。
examples.pinyin: Huǒtuǐ hé jīdàn shì hěn chángjiàn de zǎocān.
examples.english: Ham and eggs are a very common breakfast.

examples.hanzi: 这块火腿太咸了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài huǒtuǐ tài xián le.
examples.english: This piece of ham is too salty.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 别: 制 is cutting to shape, then to make and to control.
止 (stop) — a picture of a foot planted on the ground: where the foot stops. Seen in 步 step (two feet) and 正 correct.

example.hanzi: 警察及时制止了这场斗殴。
example.pinyin: jǐngchá jíshí zhìzhǐle zhè chǎng dòu'ōu.
example.english: The police stopped the fight in time.
example.fact: Stock exchanges use automatic 'circuit breakers' that halt trading for a set period if a major index falls by a certain percentage in a single day. The mechanism was introduced in the United States after the 1987 Black Monday crash to curb panic selling.

examples.hanzi: 老师立刻制止了他们的吵闹。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī lìkè zhìzhǐ le tāmen de chǎonào.
examples.english: The teacher immediately put a stop to their noise.

examples.hanzi: 我们要制止浪费粮食的行为。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào zhìzhǐ làngfèi liángshi de xíngwéi.
examples.english: We should stop the wasting of food.

components.note: 石 (stone) — marks stones and minerals, as in 碎 shatter, 破 break, 磨 grind; 磕 is knocking against something hard.
盍 (hé) — loose sound hint (kē vs hé); same part in 嗑 kè.

example.hanzi: 我的头磕到桌子上了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de tóu kē dào zhuōzi shang le.
example.english: I bumped my head on the table.
example.fact: 磕 is colloquial: 磕头 (kowtow), 磕磕绊绊 (stumbling), 磕巴 (stammer). In the north, 磕瓜子 means cracking sunflower seeds with the teeth.

examples.hanzi: 他不小心把膝盖磕破了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn bǎ xīgài kē pò le.
examples.english: He accidentally scraped his knee.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶在磕瓜子。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai zài kē guāzǐ.
examples.english: Grandma is cracking sunflower seeds.

components.note: 刂 (knife; 刀) — marks cutting, as in 别 separate, 刻 carve, 划 slice; 剃 is shaving with a blade.
弟 (dì) — close sound: 剃 tì. 弟 also sounds out 梯 tī and 第 dì.

example.hanzi: 他把胡子剃掉了。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ húzi tì diào le.
example.english: He shaved off his beard.
example.fact: 剃 appears in 剃头 (to shave the head) and 剃须刀 (razor). The Qing 剃发令 of 1645 forced men to shave their foreheads and wear a queue.

examples.hanzi: 他每天早上剃胡子。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān zǎoshang tì húzi.
examples.english: He shaves every morning.

examples.hanzi: 理发师把他的头发剃短了。
examples.pinyin: Lǐfàshī bǎ tā de tóufa tì duǎn le.
examples.english: The barber shaved his hair short.

components.note: 心 (heart) — marks feelings and thought, as in 想 think, 念 miss, 感 feel; 憋 is holding in a feeling or breath.
敝 (bì) — loose sound hint (biē); same part in 蔽 bì and 弊 bì.

example.hanzi: 他憋了一肚子气。
example.pinyin: Tā biē le yí dùzi qì.
example.english: He's bottled up a lot of anger.
example.fact: 憋 is colloquial: 憋气 (hold one's breath), 憋尿 (hold in urine) and 憋屈 (feel wronged). It has the meaning of something held in with no outlet.

examples.hanzi: 他憋着一口气潜入水里。
examples.pinyin: Tā biē zhe yì kǒu qì qiánrù shuǐ lǐ.
examples.english: He held his breath and dived into the water.

examples.hanzi: 有话就说，别憋在心里。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu huà jiù shuō, bié biē zài xīnlǐ.
examples.english: If you have something to say, say it, and don't hold it in.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 经过多年战乱,这个国家终于恢复了安定。
example.pinyin: jīngguò duōnián zhànluàn, zhège guójiā zhōngyú huīfùle āndìng.
example.english: After years of war, the country finally regained stability.
example.fact: A spinning gyroscope resists changes to its orientation because of a property called conservation of angular momentum. The same principle helps keep a moving bicycle upright and is used to stabilize spacecraft, ships, and camera rigs.

examples.hanzi: 他想找一份安定的工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng zhǎo yí fèn āndìng de gōngzuò.
examples.english: He wants to find a stable job.

examples.hanzi: 搬到新家后，孩子的情绪渐渐安定下来。
examples.pinyin: Bān dào xīn jiā hòu, háizi de qíngxù jiànjiàn āndìng xiàlái.
examples.english: After moving to the new home, the child gradually calmed down.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money and value, as in 财, 买, 贵; 贱 is cheap and low in value.
戋 (jiān) — near sound — 贱 is jiàn; 戋 also hints small, as in 钱 and 浅.
贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money, as in 买, 财, 费; 货 is goods that are traded.
化 (huà) — near sound — 货 is huò; 化 also sounds out 花 huā.

example.hanzi: 她在小说里骂那个反派"贱货"。
example.pinyin: tā zài xiǎoshuō lǐ mà nàge fǎnpài "jiànhuò".
example.english: In the novel, she calls the villain a "jiànhuò."
example.fact: For centuries, various legal systems classified enslaved people as property rather than persons, a practice not formally abolished in the last country to do so, Mauritania, until 1981. Estimates today suggest tens of millions of people worldwide remain trapped in forms of forced labor.

examples.hanzi: 别用“贱货”这种脏话骂人。
examples.pinyin: Bié yòng "jiànhuò" zhè zhǒng zānghuà mà rén.
examples.english: Don't curse at people with a foul word like "jiànhuò".

examples.hanzi: 这个词是一句很难听的骂人话，“贱货”。
examples.pinyin: Zhège cí shì yí jù hěn nántīng de mà rén huà, "jiànhuò".
examples.english: This is a very ugly insult: "jiànhuò".

components.note: 门 (gate) — a picture of a two-leaf door; as a radical it frames characters of doors and openings — 开, 关, 问, 间.
钅 (metal, from 金) — marks metals, as in 铁, 钱, 银; 锁 is a metal lock. The right side matches 琐 suǒ and 唢 suǒ.

example.hanzi: 我们换了新的门锁。
example.pinyin: wǒmen huànle xīn de ménsuǒ.
example.english: We changed to a new door lock.
example.fact: Ancient Egyptians developed the earliest known pin-lock mechanism around 4,000 years ago, made from wood. The same basic pin-tumbler principle, later refined by Linus Yale Jr. in the 1860s, is still used in most standard door locks today.

examples.hanzi: 门锁坏了，我打不开门。
examples.pinyin: Ménsuǒ huài le, wǒ dǎ bù kāi mén.
examples.english: The door lock is broken and I can't open the door.

examples.hanzi: 出门前记得检查一下门锁。
examples.pinyin: Chūmén qián jìde jiǎnchá yíxià ménsuǒ.
examples.english: Remember to check the door lock before leaving.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 伙 is a companion.
火 (huǒ, fire) gives the exact sound; 火 also means fire.

example.hanzi: 那个小伙很有礼貌。
example.pinyin: nàge xiǎohuǒ hěn yǒu lǐmào.
example.english: That young guy is very polite.
example.fact: In Japan, Coming of Age Day (Seijin no Hi) is a national holiday held on the second Monday of January, celebrating everyone who turned 20 during the previous year. Many young women mark the occasion by wearing an elaborate furisode kimono.

examples.hanzi: 这个小伙干活很勤快。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎohuǒ gànhuó hěn qínkuai.
examples.english: This young guy works very diligently.

examples.hanzi: 几个小伙在球场上打篮球。
examples.pinyin: Jǐ gè xiǎohuǒ zài qiúchǎng shàng dǎ lánqiú.
examples.english: A few young guys are playing basketball on the court.

meanings: an exciting turn of events (to watch unfold)

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
戈 (halberd) — weapons, as in 战 war and 成; the traditional 戲 was a play or contest.

example.hanzi: 好戏还在后头呢。
example.pinyin: hǎoxì hái zài hòutou ne.
example.english: The best part of the show is still to come.
example.fact: London's Globe Theatre, where many of Shakespeare's plays premiered starting in 1599, could hold up to 3,000 spectators standing in the open-air yard around the stage. The original building burned down in 1613 after a stage cannon ignited its thatched roof.

examples.hanzi: 这场球赛真是好戏连台。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng qiúsài zhēn shì hǎoxì liántái.
examples.english: This match was a great show from start to finish.

examples.hanzi: 大家都在等着看好戏。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu zài děngzhe kàn hǎoxì.
examples.english: Everyone is waiting to see the fun unfold.

components.note: 后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).
月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the flesh/body radical (月 in 脸, 脚, 肚); 背 is the back of the body.
北 (běi) — near sound — 背 is bèi; 北 originally pictured two people back to back, which is the sense of 背.

example.hanzi: 他的后背被太阳晒得又红又痛。
example.pinyin: tā de hòubèi bèi tàiyáng shàide yòu hóng yòu tòng.
example.english: His back was burned red and sore by the sun.
example.fact: The human spine has 33 vertebrae at birth, but several fuse together in the sacrum and coccyx by adulthood, leaving 26 movable bones. It is also naturally curved in an S-shape, which helps absorb shock while walking or running.

examples.hanzi: 他的后背靠在椅子上。
examples.pinyin: Tā de hòubèi kào zài yǐzi shàng.
examples.english: His back leaned against the chair.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈轻轻拍着宝宝的后背。
examples.pinyin: Māma qīngqīng pāizhe bǎobao de hòubèi.
examples.english: Mom gently pats the baby on the back.

components.note: 身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.
高 (tall) — a drawing of a tall tower building. 高 also sounds out 糕 gāo (cake), 搞 gǎo and 稿 gǎo.

example.hanzi: 他的身高超过一米九。
example.pinyin: tā de shēngāo chāoguò yī mǐ jiǔ.
example.english: His height is over 1.9 meters.
example.fact: Robert Wadlow, the tallest man ever medically documented, reached 2.72 meters (8 feet 11 inches) before his death in 1940 at age 22. His extraordinary growth was caused by a pituitary gland disorder that led to excessive growth hormone production.

examples.hanzi: 你的身高有多少？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shēngāo yǒu duōshao?
examples.english: How tall are you?

examples.hanzi: 孩子的身高一年比一年高。
examples.pinyin: Háizi de shēngāo yì nián bǐ yì nián gāo.
examples.english: The child grows taller every year.

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
大 (big) — an extra stroke below emphasises it: bigger than big, too much. 太 also sounds out 泰 tài.
大 (big) — an extra stroke below emphasises it: bigger than big, too much. 太 also sounds out 泰 tài.

example.hanzi: 一位老太太正在公园里散步。
example.pinyin: yī wèi lǎotàitai zhèngzài gōngyuán lǐ sànbù.
example.english: An elderly lady is taking a walk in the park.
example.fact: Jeanne Calment of France holds the verified record for the longest confirmed human lifespan, living to 122 years and 164 days before her death in 1997. Her record has stood for decades despite continued advances in healthcare and life expectancy.

examples.hanzi: 这位老太太每天早上都打太极拳。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎotàitai měi tiān zǎoshang dōu dǎ tàijíquán.
examples.english: This old lady does tai chi every morning.

examples.hanzi: 我扶着老太太过了马路。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ fúzhe lǎotàitai guò le mǎlù.
examples.english: I helped the old lady cross the street.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — paying to buy back; also in 财 wealth, 买 buy.
卖 (mài) is a stand-in for an older sound; the same part appears in 读 dú and 续 xù.
今 (jīn) — the top part hints the sound — 金 is jīn, like 今; 金 means gold and metal.
金 (metal) — as a radical it shrinks to 钅 in simplified characters — 钱 money, 铁 iron, 钟 clock, 银 silver.

example.hanzi: 绑匪要求支付一百万美元的赎金。
example.pinyin: bǎngfěi yāoqiú zhīfù yī bǎiwàn měiyuán de shújīn.
example.english: The kidnappers demanded a one-million-dollar ransom.
example.fact: King Richard the Lionheart of England was captured in 1192 while returning from the Crusades, and his release required a ransom of roughly 150,000 marks, an amount so large that England's treasury needed years of special taxation to raise it.

examples.hanzi: 家属已经把赎金交给了绑匪。
examples.pinyin: Jiāshǔ yǐjīng bǎ shújīn jiāo gěi le bǎngfěi.
examples.english: The family has already handed the ransom to the kidnappers.

examples.hanzi: 电影里的海盗要求一大笔赎金。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de hǎidào yāoqiú yí dà bǐ shújīn.
examples.english: The pirates in the movie demand a large ransom.

components.note: 心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.
火 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 灯 lamp, 烧 burn, 热 hot: a hot, fevered head, hence vexed.
页 (head) is a loose sound clue for fán; as a meaning part 页 means head or page.

example.hanzi: 最近的工作压力让他很心烦。
example.pinyin: zuìjìn de gōngzuò yālì ràng tā hěn xīnfán.
example.english: Recent work pressure has left him feeling very agitated.
example.fact: Chronic stress triggers sustained release of cortisol, a hormone that helps the body respond to short-term danger but, when elevated for long periods, has been linked to impaired memory, weakened immune function, and increased cardiovascular risk.

examples.hanzi: 孩子哭个不停，让妈妈很心烦。
examples.pinyin: Háizi kū gè bù tíng, ràng māma hěn xīnfán.
examples.english: The child won't stop crying, which makes Mom upset.

examples.hanzi: 别来烦我，我现在心烦着呢。
examples.pinyin: Bié lái fán wǒ, wǒ xiànzài xīnfán zhe ne.
examples.english: Don't bother me; I'm feeling irritated right now.

components.note: 言 (speech) — 言 is the traditional full form of the 讠 radical for speech and language: 说, 话, 语, 请.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and discussion: 说, 议, 谈; 论 is debate and theory.
仑 (lún) gives the sound; same part in 轮 lún and 伦 lún.

example.hanzi: 宪法保障公民的言论自由。
example.pinyin: xiànfǎ bǎozhàng gōngmín de yánlùn zìyóu.
example.english: The constitution guarantees citizens' freedom of speech.
example.fact: The First Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, ratified in 1791, prohibits Congress from abridging freedom of speech. The amendment restrains government action specifically, a distinction that leaves private companies and employers free to set their own speech rules.

examples.hanzi: 网上的言论不一定都是真的。
examples.pinyin: Wǎngshàng de yánlùn bù yídìng dōu shì zhēn de.
examples.english: Opinions online are not necessarily all true.

examples.hanzi: 他发表了一些不当言论，受到了批评。
examples.pinyin: Tā fābiǎo le yìxiē búdàng yánlùn, shòudào le pīpíng.
examples.english: He made some inappropriate remarks and was criticized.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤; water means life: 活 is alive.
舌 (shé, tongue) is a loose sound clue for huó; also in 话 huà.
讠 (speech) — words, as in 说, 请, 谢: 该 is what one ought to say or do.
亥 (hài) is a close sound clue for gāi; 亥 also sounds out 孩 hái, 核 hé and 刻 kè.

example.hanzi: 他自己不小心摔倒了,活该。
example.pinyin: tā zìjǐ bù xiǎoxīn shuāidǎole, huógāi.
example.english: He fell because of his own carelessness — serves him right.
example.fact: Schadenfreude, the pleasure derived from another person's misfortune, has been studied by psychologists as a distinct emotion tied to envy or a sense of justice. Brain-imaging studies show it activates reward centers similar to those triggered by personal achievement.

examples.hanzi: 谁让你不听劝，活该！
examples.pinyin: Shéi ràng nǐ bù tīng quàn, huógāi!
examples.english: Serves you right for not listening to advice!

examples.hanzi: 他迟到被老板批评，真是活该。
examples.pinyin: Tā chídào bèi lǎobǎn pīpíng, zhēnshi huógāi.
examples.english: He was late and got scolded by the boss; he deserved it.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo strips, once written on, as in 笔, 等, 管: a slip, so simple and brief.
间 (jiān) is a close sound clue for jiǎn.
力 (lì) sounds exactly like 历 — simplified 历 replaced complex 歷 with 力 for the sound; meaning is passing through time.

example.hanzi: 我正在修改我的简历。
example.pinyin: wǒ zhèngzài xiūgǎi wǒ de jiǎnlì.
example.english: I am revising my résumé.
example.fact: The résumé is sometimes traced back to Leonardo da Vinci, who in 1482 wrote a letter listing his skills and accomplishments to seek employment with the Duke of Milan, though the modern one-page résumé format did not become standard until the 20th century.

examples.hanzi: 申请工作要先写一份简历。
examples.pinyin: Shēnqǐng gōngzuò yào xiān xiě yí fèn jiǎnlì.
examples.english: To apply for a job you first need to write a résumé.

examples.hanzi: 请把你的简历发到我的邮箱。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ nǐ de jiǎnlì fā dào wǒ de yóuxiāng.
examples.english: Please send your résumé to my email.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — crops and harvests: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 利 shows grain 禾 cut with a blade 刂, hence profit and sharp.
氵 (water) — moisture; also in 河 river, 海 sea.
闰 (rùn) gives the exact sound.

example.hanzi: 这家公司今年的利润大幅增长。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā gōngsī jīnnián de lìrùn dàfú zēngzhǎng.
example.english: This company's profits have grown significantly this year.
example.fact: Standard Oil, founded by John D. Rockefeller in 1870, at its peak controlled about 90 percent of U.S. oil refining capacity. Its profits grew so large that the U.S. Supreme Court ordered the company broken into 34 separate firms in 1911 under antitrust law.

examples.hanzi: 这家小店每个月的利润不多。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā xiǎo diàn měi gè yuè de lìrùn bù duō.
examples.english: This little shop doesn't make much profit each month.

examples.hanzi: 他们靠卖水果赚取利润。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen kào mài shuǐguǒ zhuànqǔ lìrùn.
examples.english: They make a profit by selling fruit.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — a fitting feeling; also in 快 happy, 情 feeling.
合 (hé) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 洽 qià, as in 洽谈.
當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).

example.hanzi: 请选择一个恰当的词来填空。
example.pinyin: qǐng xuǎnzé yī gè qiàdàng de cí lái tiánkòng.
example.english: Please choose an appropriate word to fill in the blank.
example.fact: Astronomers use the term 'Goldilocks zone' to describe the range of distances from a star where a planet's temperature is just right for liquid water to exist on its surface — neither too hot nor too cold — a key factor in the search for potentially habitable exoplanets.

examples.hanzi: 他的回答既简短又恰当。
examples.pinyin: Tā de huídá jì jiǎnduǎn yòu qiàdàng.
examples.english: His answer was both brief and appropriate.

examples.hanzi: 在这种场合穿牛仔裤不太恰当。
examples.pinyin: Zài zhè zhǒng chǎnghé chuān niúzǎikù bú tài qiàdàng.
examples.english: Wearing jeans on this kind of occasion is not quite appropriate.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — pushing aside by hand; also in 推 push, 拉 pull.
发 (fā) is only a loose clue; it also sounds out 泼 pō.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.

example.hanzi: 如果有紧急情况,请拨打这个电话号码。
example.pinyin: rúguǒ yǒu jǐnjí qíngkuàng, qǐng bōdǎ zhège diànhuà hàomǎ.
example.english: If there is an emergency, please dial this phone number.
example.fact: The 911 emergency number was first introduced in the United States in 1968, in Haleyville, Alabama, replacing a patchwork of local emergency numbers. It was chosen partly because it was short, easy to remember, and had not previously been used as an area code or service code.

examples.hanzi: 我拨打了三次，他都没接电话。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bōdǎ le sān cì, tā dōu méi jiē diànhuà.
examples.english: I dialed three times, and he didn't pick up.

examples.hanzi: 请拨打客服热线咨询。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bōdǎ kèfú rèxiàn zīxún.
examples.english: Please call the customer service hotline for inquiries.

components.note: 阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 住.
立 (stand) — the spot where a person 亻 stands 立: a position or seat; also 位置 position.

example.hanzi: 医生检查了受伤的部位。
example.pinyin: yīshēng jiǎnchále shòushāng de bùwèi.
example.english: The doctor examined the injured part of the body.
example.fact: Proprioception, the sense of where your body parts are in space without looking, relies on specialized sensory receptors in muscles and joints called proprioceptors. It is what allows you to touch your nose with your eyes closed.

examples.hanzi: 他的身体哪个部位疼？
examples.pinyin: Tā de shēntǐ nǎge bùwèi téng?
examples.english: Which part of his body hurts?

examples.hanzi: 车的这个部位容易生锈。
examples.pinyin: Chē de zhège bùwèi róngyì shēngxiù.
examples.english: This part of the car rusts easily.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 传 is something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 传 is chuán; 专 also sounds out 转 zhuǎn and 砖 zhuān.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.hanzi: 远处传来了阵阵歌声。
example.pinyin: yuǎnchù chuánláile zhènzhèn gēshēng.
example.english: Bursts of singing came drifting from a distance.
example.fact: Sound travels roughly four times faster through water than through air, at about 1,480 meters per second compared to 343 meters per second. This is why underwater listening devices called hydrophones can detect whale calls from many kilometers away.

examples.hanzi: 隔壁传来了一阵吵闹声。
examples.pinyin: Gébì chuánlái le yí zhèn chǎonào shēng.
examples.english: A burst of noisy sound came from next door.

examples.hanzi: 这个好消息很快就传来了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège hǎo xiāoxi hěn kuài jiù chuánlái le.
examples.english: This good news arrived very quickly.

meanings: Rus' (as in Kievan Rus' 基輔羅斯|基辅罗斯[Ji1 fu3 Luo2 si1])

components.note: 罒 (net) — 罒 is a net, as in 罚, 置; 罗 is a net, and is mostly seen in 罗马 Rome.
斤 (axe) — the original idea was chopping with an axe, as in 新, 斩 chop, 断 break; today 斯 is mostly a sound-borrowing syllable sī in foreign names like 俄罗斯.

example.hanzi: 罗斯是我们班上新来的交换生。
example.pinyin: Luósī shì wǒmen bān shàng xīnlái de jiāohuàn shēng.
example.english: Ross is the new exchange student in our class.
example.fact: Kievan Rus' was a medieval federation of Slavic and Finnic peoples that emerged around the 9th century, centered on the city of Kyiv. Historians consider it the common ancestor of the modern nations of Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus.

examples.hanzi: 罗斯是我大学时的好朋友。
examples.pinyin: Luósī shì wǒ dàxué shí de hǎo péngyou.
examples.english: Ross was a good friend of mine in college.

examples.hanzi: 今天罗斯要给我们讲一个故事。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān Luósī yào gěi wǒmen jiǎng yí gè gùshi.
examples.english: Today Ross is going to tell us a story.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 河 river, 汤 soup; 漆 is lacquer, a liquid sap, as in 油漆 paint.

example.hanzi: 他想把门漆成红色。
example.pinyin: Tā xiǎng bǎ mén qī chéng hóngsè.
example.english: He wants to paint the door red.
example.fact: 漆 is lacquer from the sap of the lacquer tree, used in China for thousands of years (漆器). 油漆 is paint, and 漆黑 means pitch black.

examples.hanzi: 墙上刷了一层白漆。
examples.pinyin: Qiáng shàng shuā le yì céng báiqī.
examples.english: The wall has been painted with a coat of white paint.

examples.hanzi: 屋里一片漆黑，什么都看不见。
examples.pinyin: Wū lǐ yí piàn qīhēi, shénme dōu kàn bu jiàn.
examples.english: It is pitch black inside, and nothing can be seen.

components.note: 欠 (yawn, open mouth) — breath and mouth actions, as in 歌 song, 吹 blow.
又 here replaces 雚 (huān) in the traditional 歡, so it is only a stand-in; same shorthand in 观 and 劝.

example.hanzi: 我很喜欢这首歌。
example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xǐhuan zhè shǒu gē.
example.english: I really like this song.
example.fact: 欢 appears in 喜欢 (like), 欢迎 (welcome), 欢乐 (joy), 欢呼 (cheer). In 喜欢 it takes a neutral tone.

examples.hanzi: 欢迎大家来到我们学校。
examples.pinyin: Huānyíng dàjiā láidào wǒmen xuéxiào.
examples.english: Welcome everyone to our school.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们看到礼物都很欢喜。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen kàndào lǐwù dōu hěn huānxǐ.
examples.english: The children were all delighted to see the gifts.

meanings: to be up to a task

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 脑, 脚, 肚; here part of the simplified form 胜 for victory.
生 (shēng) is a near sound match for shèng; also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 任 is a duty a person bears.
壬 (rén) gives the same sound, different tone; also in 妊 rèn.

example.hanzi: 他完全能够胜任这项工作。
example.pinyin: tā wánquán nénggòu shèngrèn zhè xiàng gōngzuò.
example.english: He is fully qualified for this job.
example.fact: NASA's astronaut selection process accepts fewer than 0.2% of applicants, screening tens of thousands of candidates for the small number of positions needed to crew the International Space Station. Even after selection, candidates undergo roughly two years of training before being certified qualified for spaceflight duty.

examples.hanzi: 她刚毕业，还不能胜任这个职位。
examples.pinyin: Tā gāng bìyè, hái bù néng shèngrèn zhège zhíwèi.
examples.english: She just graduated and can't yet handle this position.

examples.hanzi: 我相信你能胜任经理的工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiāngxìn nǐ néng shèngrèn jīnglǐ de gōngzuò.
examples.english: I believe you can handle the manager's job.

components.note: 手 (hand) — over 目 (eye): a hand shading the eyes to look into the distance. 目 marks seeing words, as in 眼, 睡.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.

example.hanzi: 妈妈让我看好弟弟，别让他乱跑。
example.pinyin: māma ràng wǒ kānhǎo dìdi, bié ràng tā luàn pǎo.
example.english: Mom told me to keep an eye on my little brother so he doesn't run off.
example.fact: Lifeguards are trained to scan their assigned zone every ten seconds and reach any swimmer within twenty to thirty seconds, a rule known as the 10/20 principle. Drowning can happen silently in under a minute, without the loud thrashing shown in movies.

examples.hanzi: 大家都很看好这个年轻人。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu hěn kànhǎo zhège niánqīngrén.
examples.english: Everyone is optimistic about this young man.

examples.hanzi: 很多人看好这家公司的前景。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō rén kànhǎo zhè jiā gōngsī de qiánjǐng.
examples.english: Many people are bullish on this company's prospects.

meanings: fat (in the body, in a plant, or in food)

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body and flesh, as in 肥 fat, 脸 face; 脂 is fat.
旨 (zhǐ) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 指 zhǐ.
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body and flesh, as in 肥 fat, 脸 face; 肪 is animal fat.
方 (fāng) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 房 fáng and 防 fáng.

example.hanzi: 橄榄油含有大量对心脏有益的脂肪。
example.pinyin: gǎnlǎnyóu hányǒu dàliàng duì xīnzàng yǒuyì de zhīfáng.
example.english: Olive oil contains a large amount of fat that is good for the heart.
example.fact: Blue whales carry a layer of blubber up to 20 centimeters thick that insulates them in freezing polar waters and stores enough energy to fuel migrations of over 8,000 kilometers without feeding. This fat reserve is central to how the largest animals on Earth survive months between meals.

examples.hanzi: 吃太多油炸食品会让身体长脂肪。
examples.pinyin: Chī tài duō yóuzhá shípǐn huì ràng shēntǐ zhǎng zhīfáng.
examples.english: Eating too much fried food makes the body gain fat.

examples.hanzi: 他想减掉身上的脂肪，所以开始跑步。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng jiǎn diào shēnshang de zhīfáng, suǒyǐ kāishǐ pǎobù.
examples.english: He wants to lose body fat, so he started running.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting something in two, hence a second or secondary one.
畐 (fú) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 富 fù, 福 fú and 幅 fú.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.
用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).

example.hanzi: 这种药可能有轻微的副作用。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǒng yào kěnéng yǒu qīngwēi de fùzuòyòng.
example.english: This medicine may have mild side effects.
example.fact: In the late 1950s, the sedative thalidomide was prescribed to pregnant women for morning sickness before its severe side effect — causing birth defects in thousands of infants — was discovered. The disaster led directly to the strict drug-safety testing requirements used worldwide today.

examples.hanzi: 这种药没有什么副作用。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào méiyǒu shénme fùzuòyòng.
examples.english: This medicine has no side effects.

examples.hanzi: 吃了感冒药以后，我觉得有点困，这是副作用。
examples.pinyin: Chī le gǎnmàoyào yǐhòu, wǒ juéde yǒudiǎn kùn, zhè shì fùzuòyòng.
examples.english: After taking the cold medicine I felt sleepy, which is a side effect.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — scattered raindrops, hence small bits and nothing; also in 雪 snow, 雷 thunder.
令 (lìng) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 铃 líng, 龄 líng and 领 lǐng.
钅 (metal) — 钅 is the simplified 金 (metal), as in 铁, 银, 钟; early money was metal coins.
戋 (jiān) — near sound — 钱 is qián; 戋 also sounds out 浅 qiǎn and 线 xiàn, and means small or thin.

example.hanzi: 我口袋里只有一些零钱。
example.pinyin: wǒ kǒudài lǐ zhǐyǒu yìxiē língqián.
example.english: I only have some small change in my pocket.
example.fact: The U.S. Mint estimates that Americans keep roughly $60 billion worth of coins sitting unused in jars, drawers, and couch cushions rather than in circulation. That much idle change is one reason the Federal Reserve periodically has to order fresh coin production to keep up with demand.

examples.hanzi: 我身上没有零钱，能扫码付款吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shēnshang méiyǒu língqián, néng sǎomǎ fùkuǎn ma?
examples.english: I have no small change; can I pay by scanning a code?

examples.hanzi: 这些零钱是我攒着买玩具的。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē língqián shì wǒ zǎnzhe mǎi wánjù de.
examples.english: I've been saving this small change to buy toys.

components.note: 自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).
贝 (cowry shell, money) — 责 first meant demanding payment of a debt, hence duty. 责 sounds out 债 zhài, 积 jī and 绩 jì.

example.hanzi: 考试没考好，他一直在自责。
example.pinyin: kǎoshì méi kǎohǎo, tā yīzhí zài zìzé.
example.english: He kept blaming himself after doing poorly on the exam.
example.fact: Survivor guilt, first documented among concentration camp survivors and later studied in soldiers and disaster survivors, describes intense self-blame felt by people who lived through an event that others did not — even when they had no ability to change the outcome.

examples.hanzi: 他为自己犯的错误深深自责。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèi zìjǐ fàn de cuòwù shēnshēn zìzé.
examples.english: He blames himself deeply for the mistake he made.

examples.hanzi: 别太自责了，这不是你的错。
examples.pinyin: Bié tài zìzé le, zhè bú shì nǐ de cuò.
examples.english: Don't blame yourself too much; it isn't your fault.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 她对流浪动物充满同情心。
example.pinyin: tā duì liúlàng dòngwù chōngmǎn tóngqíngxīn.
example.english: She is full of compassion for stray animals.
example.fact: Elephants have been observed standing vigil over the bodies of dead herd members, touching the bones with their trunks and feet for long periods. Researchers cite this behavior as evidence of empathy and grief in a species outside our own.

examples.hanzi: 我们应该对老人有同情心。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi duì lǎorén yǒu tóngqíngxīn.
examples.english: We should have compassion for the elderly.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子很有同情心，常常帮助同学。
examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi hěn yǒu tóngqíngxīn, chángcháng bāngzhù tóngxué.
examples.english: This child is very caring and often helps classmates.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 运 is to move, then to be moved by luck.
云 (yún) is a near sound match for yùn.
车 (cart) — 车 is a cart or vehicle, as in 轮, 输, 车; 转 is turning of wheels.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 转 is zhuǎn; 专 also sounds out 传 chuán and 砖 zhuān.

example.hanzi: 这台机器一直运转正常。
example.pinyin: zhè tái jīqì yīzhí yùnzhuǎn zhèngcháng.
example.english: This machine has been running normally.
example.fact: The Earth completes one full rotation every 23 hours, 56 minutes, and 4 seconds — slightly short of 24 hours. That is why a sidereal day, measured against distant stars, runs a few minutes faster than the familiar solar day.

examples.hanzi: 工厂的机器二十四小时运转。
examples.pinyin: Gōngchǎng de jīqì èrshísì xiǎoshí yùnzhuǎn.
examples.english: The factory's machines run twenty-four hours a day.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司运转得很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī yùnzhuǎn de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This company is running very well.

components.note: 彳 (step) — walking, as in 行, 往, 得.
艮 (gèn) is a close sound clue for hěn; 艮 also sounds out 跟 gēn, 根 gēn, 恨 hèn and 银 yín.
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) — 难 was first the name of a bird; "hard" is a borrowed use. The 又 here stands in for the traditional left part.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.

example.hanzi: 这件事最后会怎样，现在很难说。
example.pinyin: zhè jiàn shì zuìhòu huì zěnyàng, xiànzài hěn nán shuō.
example.english: It's hard to say how this will turn out in the end.
example.fact: Meteorologist Edward Lorenz discovered in the 1960s that tiny rounding differences in his weather simulations produced wildly different forecasts, giving rise to chaos theory and the popular 'butterfly effect.' It remains a key reason weather forecasts grow unreliable beyond about ten days.

examples.hanzi: 他明天来不来，我也很难说。
examples.pinyin: Tā míngtiān lái bu lái, wǒ yě hěn nán shuō.
examples.english: Whether he'll come tomorrow, I can't really say.

examples.hanzi: 这两个方案哪个好，很难说。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè fāng'àn nǎge hǎo, hěn nán shuō.
examples.english: It's hard to say which of these two plans is better.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).
戈 (halberd, weapon) — war and weapons: 我, 成, 武, 伐; here fighting.
占 (zhàn) sounds exactly like 战; also in 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 两国之间随时可能开战。
example.pinyin: liǎng guó zhījiān suíshí kěnéng kāizhàn.
example.english: War could break out between the two countries at any moment.
example.fact: The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896 is recorded as history's shortest war, lasting only about 38 minutes between the British Empire and the Sultanate of Zanzibar before the sultan's forces surrendered.

examples.hanzi: 两个国家宣布正式开战了。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng gè guójiā xuānbù zhèngshì kāizhàn le.
examples.english: The two countries officially announced they were going to war.

examples.hanzi: 比赛还没开战，场上气氛已经很紧张。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài hái méi kāizhàn, chǎng shàng qìfēn yǐjīng hěn jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: The match hadn't started, but the atmosphere on the field was already tense.

components.note: 穴 (hole, cave) — 穴 marks holes and cavities, as in 空, 穷, 突; 窗 is an opening in a wall.
囱 (cōng) — near sound — 窗 is chuāng; 囱 also sounds out 葱 cōng and 聪 cōng.
巾 (cloth) — a hanging cloth, as in 布 cloth, 帽 hat; 帘 is a curtain.

example.hanzi: 请把窗帘拉上，外面太亮了。
example.pinyin: qǐng bǎ chuānglián lā shàng, wàimiàn tài liàng le.
example.english: Please close the curtains, it's too bright outside.
example.fact: During World War II, Britain's blackout regulations required households to cover every window with heavy curtains or black paper after dark, so that no light could guide enemy bombers to cities. Wardens patrolled the streets at night to enforce compliance.

examples.hanzi: 我们给客厅挂了新窗帘。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gěi kètīng guà le xīn chuānglián.
examples.english: We hung new curtains in the living room.

examples.hanzi: 风吹动了窗帘，一只小鸟飞了进来。
examples.pinyin: Fēng chuīdòng le chuānglián, yì zhī xiǎo niǎo fēi le jìnlái.
examples.english: The wind stirred the curtain and a little bird flew in.

components.note: 刀 (knife, written 刂 on the right) — cutting, as in 分 divide, 刻 carve, 到 arrive.
七 (qī) is a close sound clue for qiē/qiè.
廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).

example.hanzi: 医生小心地把伤口切开。
example.pinyin: yīshēng xiǎoxīn de bǎ shāngkǒu qiē kāi.
example.english: The doctor carefully cut the wound open.
example.fact: Before general anesthesia was introduced in the 1840s, surgeons operated on fully conscious patients and valued speed above all. Scottish surgeon Robert Liston was famous for amputating a leg in under 30 seconds to minimize the patient's suffering.

examples.hanzi: 请把苹果切开，分给大家。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ píngguǒ qiēkāi, fēn gěi dàjiā.
examples.english: Please cut the apple open and share it with everyone.

examples.hanzi: 他把西瓜切开，里面又红又甜。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ xīguā qiēkāi, lǐmiàn yòu hóng yòu tián.
examples.english: He cut the watermelon open, and it was red and sweet inside.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 改, 放: to gather by force or hand.
丩 (jiū) is only a loose sound clue for shōu.
见 (see) — seeing and looking, as in 现, 觉, 看: 视 is to look.
礻 here is 示 (shì), the altar radical in 礼 and 神: in 视 it is the exact sound clue.
幺 (tiny thread) — the dictionary story is a cord pulled taut in a frame, so 'to lead'; another account sees a bird net. Origin is disputed.
十 (ten) — the lower bar. Reads shuài to lead (率领) and lǜ for rate (效率, 比率). Memory aid: ten threads pulled together as a rate.

example.hanzi: 这部剧的收视率一直很高。
example.pinyin: zhè bù jù de shōushìlǜ yīzhí hěn gāo.
example.english: This drama's ratings have consistently been high.
example.fact: Super Bowl LVIII in 2024 drew roughly 123 million U.S. viewers, making it the most-watched television broadcast in American history and surpassing the 1969 Apollo 11 moon landing telecast.

examples.hanzi: 这个节目的收视率越来越低。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jiémù de shōushìlǜ yuèláiyuè dī.
examples.english: This show's ratings keep getting lower.

examples.hanzi: 电视台很关心新剧的收视率。
examples.pinyin: Diànshìtái hěn guānxīn xīn jù de shōushìlǜ.
examples.english: The TV station cares a lot about the new series' ratings.
